top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) rest on a distinct idea, magic-wavelength trapping, which cancels the clock-transition light shift while many neutral atoms are interrogated at once; this differs in kind from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes. The 1e-18 accuracy is demonstrated and reproduced by independent laboratories, and the two-name allocation avoids an arbitrary exclusion. A narrow citation limited to demonstrated performance handles the overlap concern. P002 is a close second: it is conceptually broader, but the three-name limit omits Hasan and Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang. P003 is third because the experimental credit omits the first authors of the 2018 papers and the field is still moving.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my astroparticle and CERN background is closer to B043 and B019, which are not in the slate, and I have no documented tie to Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer
